question.worked_solution:
Recall that if $X=[{X}_{1},{X}_{2},…,{X}_{k}]^{T}$ is a multivariate normal random vector with mean vector $\mu $ and covariance matrix $Σ,$ then the random variable $Y,$ defined as

$$
Y={c}^{T}X={\sum }_{i=1}^{k}{c}_{i}{X}_{i}
$$

is a normally distributed random variable, where $c$ is any $k\times 1$ column vector, and  

$$
\begin{aligned}E[Y] & ={c}^{T}\mu , \\ Var[Y] & ={c}^{T}Σc.\end{aligned}
$$

In our case, since we wish to know the distribution of $Y={X}_{1}+2{X}_{2}-{X}_{3},$ we have 

$$
c=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 2 \\ -1\end{aligned}].
$$

Therefore, for the mean of $Y,$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{E}[Y] & ={c}^{T}\mu  \\  & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 2 & -1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}3 \\ 1 \\ 2\end{aligned}] \\  & =3+2-2 \\  & =3,\end{aligned}
$$

and for the variance of $Y,$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{Var}[Y] & ={c}^{T}Σc \\  & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 2 & -1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}2 & 1 & 1 \\ 1 & 3 & 2 \\ 1 & 2 & 4\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}1 \\ 2 \\ -1\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 2 & -1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}3 \\ 5 \\ 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =3+10-1 \\  & =12.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, 

$$
Y∼N(3,12).
$$

Now, we need to compute $P(Y<1).$ First, transform $Y$ into a standard normal random variable $Z$ by $z$-scoring:

$$
\begin{aligned}P(Y<1) & =P(Z<\frac{1-3}{\sqrt{12}}) \\  & =P(Z<-0.58)\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we express the required probability in terms of $Φ(z):$

$$
\begin{aligned}P(Z<-0.58) & =P(Z\le -0.58) \\  & =Φ(-0.58).\end{aligned}
$$

From the table, we know that

$$
Φ(0.58)=0.7190.
$$

By the symmetry of the normal distribution, we have

$$
Φ(-0.58)=1-Φ(0.58)=1-0.7190=0.2810.
$$

As a result,

$$
\begin{aligned}P(Z<-0.58)=0.2810.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we conclude that

$$
P(Y<1)=0.2810.
$$
